questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than normal.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead on slippery roads.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow closely behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your own driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Drive at the speed limit and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep going.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross your path. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Safety belts should be:

options.text: Worn only if your vehicle does not have airbags.
Worn only on long trips.
Worn at all times while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Worn at all times while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Always wear a safety belt, even on short trips. Most crashes happen within 25 miles of home at speeds under 40 mph. Wear a safety belt even if your vehicle has airbags.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green turn protection is ending. Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass first. You may turn when the intersection is clear and traffic signals allow.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane where there is no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass.
Slow down as you pass them.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even without a marked crosswalk. Stop and let them cross safely.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Gets you to your destination faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. Speeding does not save time and leads to dangerous driving choices.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is coming.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is allowed only on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sharp right turn is coming.
questions.explanation: This yellow-green warning sign alerts you to upcoming road conditions, including curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Fewer lanes ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangle sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: You should drive at the maximum posted speed limit only:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
Under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under ideal conditions. Always drive at a safe speed and match the speed of traffic around you.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to yield to pedestrians. You can only proceed carefully if your lane is clear.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first gets the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives second gets the right-of-way.
The driver to your left always gets the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first gets the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: The first driver to reach a four-way stop has the right-of-way. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: An instructional permit allows you to:

options.text: Drive with supervision from a licensed driver over 21 years old.
Drive without supervision.
Watch another driver operate a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with supervision from a licensed driver over 21 years old.
questions.explanation: With an instructional permit, you can drive only with a licensed adult in the front seat. The adult must be at least 21 years old and have at least one year of driving experience.

questions.question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, you should:

options.text: Drive closer than you would behind a regular car.
Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Move to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind large trucks because they have larger blind spots.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing or symbols.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
At a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red traffic light. Always obey traffic officers, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in construction and work areas are:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: You want to turn right at the corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle until the person is well away from your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off water and precipitation, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, at street crossings, at railroad crossings, and in work zones. Never pass when you cannot see far enough ahead.
